title: Define a unified Call Resilience Grammar for retries, timeouts, hedging, and idempotency
creator: Sara Kim
description:
Background: Multiple teams implement ad-hoc retry and timeout logic across the serving runtime, middle-tier services, and language SDKs. Differences in semantics cause silent duplicated work (at cost), unclear failure modes during multi-region failover, and difficulty enforcing SLOs and load-shedding across layers. This work defines a single, implementable Call Resilience Grammar (CRG) that expresses: retry budgets, per-call timeouts, hedging windows, idempotency contract, and load-shedding signals.

Goals:
- Define clear client/server contract for idempotency keys (header name, TTL, dedupe behavior, response codes).
- Standardize hedged request behavior: when clients may send parallel speculative requests, how to cancel attached KV caches and how to attribute cost/metrics.
- Establish a retry budget model (tokens per caller/service) and safe defaults that respect SLOs and multi-region failover.
- Specify circuit-breaker signals and canonical load-shedding response codes so SDKs and runtime can react consistently.
- Provide migration/compatibility guidance and SDK primitives (JS/Python/Go) that make CRG actionable.

Key decisions (proposed):
- Idempotency header: X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key. Server dedupe TTL = 60s for non-streaming generation endpoints; configurable per-route.
- Idempotency semantic: server must dedupe by returned side-effect-idempotency for one write side-effect (create/update). If the server detects replay within TTL it returns 409 with body {"replay":true, "original_request_id": "..."} or returns the original success response if available.
- Hedging: Clients may issue a single hedge request after a percentile latency threshold (p95) + hedge_window (default 100ms). Hedged requests must include X-Redwood-Hedge-Basis header and be cancellable. Only the first successful non-5xx result is used; subsequent completions must be traced and billed but not returned to caller.
- Retry budget: Caller library maintains a token bucket scoped per upstream service and per-priority. Retries consume tokens; hedges consume tokens at higher cost. Token replenishment linked to successful request rates to avoid retry storms under failure.
- Circuit breakers: Breakers trip on error budgets and sustained latency. Breaker state exposed via X-Redwood-Breaker-State for observability. Open state returns HTTP 503 + Retry-After where relevant for non-idempotent calls, and 429 for soft load-shedible requests.

Instrumentation & SLO alignment:
- Every CRG-enabled call must emit structured metrics: attempt_count, hedge_sent, idempotency_key, dedupe_hit, breaker_state, consumed_retry_tokens. These map to service SLO dashboards and automated load-shedding rules.

Compatibility and migration:
- Default behaviors are conservative for backwards compatibility: hedging off by default in older SDK versions; servers must accept X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key as optional. Migration plan includes an opt-in beta flag on runtime and SDKs, a 2-week canary in dedicated region, and a 12-week rollout window.

Deliverables:
- RFC (Confluence) describing CRG and examples for text generation, embeddings, and streaming endpoints.
- Reference implementation in runtime (circuit-breaker + dedupe store + hedging coordinator).
- SDK primitives and integration tests for JS/Python/Go.
- Runbook for incident responders describing how to identify dedupe vs double-exec, how to tune retry budgets, and how to interpret breaker signals.

Why different from existing work: previous tickets standardized retry/backoff patterns but left hedging/idempotency and multi-region failure semantics under-specified. CRG is intentionally holistic (grammar) so the same spec covers SDK behavior, runtime coordination, and operator tooling for SLO-driven load shedding.
acceptance_criteria: RFC published and reviewed by runtime, SDK, and platform teams with signoffs from reliability PM and security
Reference runtime changes land behind feature flag with end-to-end test for dedupe TTL and hedging cancellation
SDKs (JS/Python/Go) expose idempotency header helpers and a hedging opt-in primitive; unit and integration tests included
Metrics emitted (attempt_count, hedge_sent, dedupe_hit, breaker_state) wired into observability dashboards and a demo SLO alert
Canary rollout executed in eu-west-1 for a 2-week period with no customer-impacting regressions; rollback plan validated
